summary:
An ISSA-sourced profile of Michigan State University's behind-the-scenes residential facilities workforce. MSU, founded in 1855 in East Lansing as a pioneer land-grant college and the first to teach scientific agriculture, spans roughly 5,200 acres, enrolls more than 51,000 students from 139 countries, all 50 states and all 83 Michigan counties, and houses about 16,000 students year-round across 27 residence halls and apartment communities totaling some 5.6 million square feet.

The piece profiles two Residence Education and Housing Services (REHS) leaders: Charles Stephens, associate director for residence hall services, who oversees the 27 residence halls, and Marque Black, associate director for university apartments and central services, who covers 1855 Place, University Village, central maintenance and food-equipment services. REHS sits within the Residential and Hospitality Services division alongside culinary, athletics, lean enterprises and assessment, and business operations.

Much of the work is invisible: food technicians service dining equipment by 6:00 a.m.; central maintenance handles key boxes during move-in and move-out, including one technician who hand-built eight wooden key holders; patching and plastering in older, "seasoned" buildings is scheduled during low-occupancy summer and spring break windows. Teams follow ISSA and APPA cleaning guidelines and apply comparable standards to maintenance, framing facility quality as a direct contributor to student learning.

On workforce issues, Stephens says the pandemic disrupted staffing as people reassessed priorities. The pair hired a dedicated trainer where none existed; that trainer was promoted to lead division-wide training, and the role is being backfilled. Black describes rebuilding morale and trust from the frontline up, using surveys, town halls and staff meetings, and acting on the feedback rather than shelving it, including working alongside crews in crawl spaces. Consistency is framed through a "one team" philosophy and the DOSE mantra, "delivering outstanding Spartan experiences," attributed to Vennie Gore.

MSU enrolls more than 51,000 students from 139 countries, all 50 states, and all 83 Michigan counties
About 16,000 students live on campus year-round
MSU housing comprises 27 residence halls and apartments totaling about 5.6 million square feet
MSU was founded in 1855 as a pioneer land-grant college and the first in the country to teach scientific agriculture
Food technicians are in dining halls by 6:00 a.m. servicing equipment
A maintenance technician built eight wooden key holders from scratch over several months
The pandemic significantly disrupted facilities staffing as workers reconsidered life priorities
The unit had no dedicated trainer before the two leaders arrived; they hired one who was then promoted to lead training for the whole division
Cleaning and maintenance follow ISSA and APPA guidelines
The DOSE philosophy, delivering outstanding Spartan experiences, was instilled by Vennie Gore
